title: 2022 building code energy and accessibility standards adopted (Queensland)
summary: Queensland phased in the NCC 2022 livable housing (accessibility) and condensation provisions from 1 October 2023 and the 7-star energy efficiency standards from 1 May 2024, the latter for houses through the Queensland Development Code, with exemptions for narrow, small and steep lots.

instruments.title: National Construction Code 2022
instruments.provisions: energy efficiency, condensation management and livable housing design provisions (Volumes One and Two, the ABCB Housing Provisions and the Livable Housing Design Standard)

instruments.title: Building Act 1975 (Qld)
instruments.provisions: s 37 (the edition of the BCA that applies), named in the Queensland schedule

instruments.title: Queensland Development Code MP 4.1 Sustainable buildings
instruments.provisions: the NCC 2022 energy efficiency (7-star) standard for houses, from 1 May 2024

commenced.what: NCC 2022 adopted as a whole; its energy efficiency, condensation management and livable housing provisions started later (the dates below)
Livable housing (accessibility) standards phased in; condensation management and the provisions for future solar, battery and electric vehicle charging equipment applied
Energy efficiency (7-star) standards applied, for houses through the Queensland Development Code MP 4.1

direction_rationale: The 2022 code raised minimum energy performance for new homes to 7 stars and added livable housing design requirements. Design and compliance costs are partly fixed per dwelling and may fall hardest on small builders, lowering entry and raising exit.
comparison: Staggered and partial adoption, October 2023 to May 2025 (NSW and WA did not adopt livable housing; Tasmania did not adopt housing energy efficiency; the NT kept 5 stars)

verified.notes: The ABCB table gives no Queensland dates; dates from the Queensland Building and Construction Commission (NCC 2022 update, and 'What's new from 1 May 2024'). The whole-edition date from the 'History of adoption' table in the NCC 2025 dataset (version 1.2). The adopting law is the one the Queensland schedule in NCC 2025 names.

assessment.summary: Adopts the 2022 National Construction Code's higher energy efficiency (7-star) and livable housing standards for new homes. Queensland adopted both, phased over 7 months, with exemptions from the accessibility standards for some lots and house styles. The standards cut running costs and improve access, which are not weighed here; they also add to the cost of building.

marks.reason: Adds design and compliance costs to every new home, which weigh most on small builders.

assessment.confidence_note: The Productivity Commission estimates housing construction regulation costs about 1% of GDP a year.

responsible.note: Produces the National Construction Code that each jurisdiction adopts.

history.what: The Australian Government announced a pause on further residential changes to the NCC until mid-2029, after NCC 2025, except essential safety and quality changes, keeping the 2022 residential standards, including 7-star energy efficiency.
